In the 2026-07-28 MCP spec, message history between distinct sampling requests is governed by the **statelessness principle**: state that needs to span multiple requests MUST be referenced by an explicit identifier the client passes on each request (source: mcp:2026-07-28/basic/index.mdx).

The protocol requires that all information needed to process a request is contained in the request itself. A server processes each request independently; no state should be inferred from previous requests, even those on the same connection or stream (source: mcp:2026-07-28/basic/index.mdx). An open connection is not a conversation or session—clients may interleave unrelated requests on the same transport (source: mcp:2026-07-28/basic/index.mdx).

Therefore, to maintain message history across sampling requests, the full conversation context must be explicitly included in each `sampling/createMessage` request rather than relying on connection state.
